errors.unavailable: This is not possible right now.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in with your passkey – no password.
login.recovery: Lost your passkey? Recovery is only possible on the server: sudo daemonica-admin recover <account>

token.label: Setup token
token.help: Create the token on the server with: sudo daemonica-admin bootstrap
token.explain: The token proves you have access to the server. It is valid for 60 minutes and is consumed when the first passkey is registered.

domain.label: Dashboard domain
domain.help: The domain's DNS record must point to this server.
domain.explain: Passkeys are bound to the domain. That is why the first passkey is registered on the final domain.

allowlist.label: Allowed networks (one address or CIDR per line)
allowlist.help: Only connections from these networks are accepted – before the TLS handshake.
allowlist.publicWarning: Public means anyone on the Internet can see and attack the login page. Fixed networks, a VPN or an SSH tunnel are recommended.
allowlist.publicConfirm: I understand the risk and want to make the dashboard publicly reachable.
allowlist.explain: The default is “allowed networks only”. Local access (127.0.0.1, ::1) always remains allowed.

certificate.acmeHelp: Free, automatically issued certificate. Port 80 must briefly be free and reachable from the Internet.
certificate.staging: Let’s Encrypt Staging (testing only, not trusted by browsers)
certificate.tos: I accept the Let’s Encrypt terms of service.
certificate.working: Issuing certificate … this can take up to a minute.
certificate.explain: The dashboard only speaks TLS 1.3. The certificate is stored only for the web service.

switch.title: Switching to the final address
switch.text: The service restarts now and will be reachable at {{url}}. Open that address and enter the token again to register your first passkey.

passkey.linuxUserHelp: File access and the terminal run with this user's permissions. root is not allowed.
passkey.noUsers: There is no regular Linux user on the server. Create one first: sudo adduser <name>
passkey.name: Passkey name (e.g. laptop)
passkey.explain: Your device creates a key pair. The private key never leaves your device; the server stores only the public key.

done.title: All set!
done.text: The dashboard is set up and you are signed in. Register a second passkey next so you cannot lock yourself out.

recovery.title: Recover access
recovery.intro: Enter the token from “sudo daemonica-admin recover” and register a new passkey.

stepup.title: Confirm with passkey
stepup.text: This action is security-relevant. Confirm it with your passkey. The confirmation is valid for 5 minutes.

overview.title: Overview
overview.empty: System overview, services, logs and processes arrive with milestone M1.1.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: Passkeys are your only sign-in method. Register at least two, e.g. laptop and phone.
passkeys.secondHint: Register a second passkey – without it, only server-side recovery helps if you lose this one.
passkeys.lastOne: The last passkey cannot be removed.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.intro: See where you are signed in and end sessions. Sessions end automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity or at the latest after 12 hours.

invite.title: Accept invitation
invite.intro: An admin invited you to Daemonica. Register your passkey now – from then on you sign in with it only.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.intro: Dashboard accounts, their roles and mapped Linux users. Changes require passkey confirmation and end the affected account's sessions.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.inviteOnce: This link is shown only now and is valid once until {{time}}. Share it over a secure channel.
accounts.inviteExplain: Daemonica creates the account without a passkey and a one-time link (valid for 60 minutes). Whoever opens the link registers the first passkey for exactly this account. The token sits in the link fragment (#), so it is not sent to the server or logged until it is redeemed. The account acts with the rights of the chosen Linux user; root can never be mapped.
accounts.confirmRole: Change the role of “{{name}}”? All sessions of this account will be ended.
accounts.confirmDelete: Type “{{name}}” to delete. Passkeys and sessions are removed; the Linux user is left unchanged.
